title: Granny rectangle
subtitle: The granny square construction extended to a two-corner rectangle
excerpt: The granny rectangle uses two corner positions instead of four, growing longer on the short sides and maintaining a fixed width. Three rounds in DK cotton produce a 7 × 14 cm tile — twice as long as a three-round granny square — for scarves, bags, and bookmark strips worked in a grid.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Crochet, Volume 2 (1887), oblong granny chapter (Internet Archive).
heroPrompt: A granny rectangle crochet motif in cream DK cotton on a pale linen background, photographed flat from above in soft daylight. Three rounds of treble clusters with two corner chain-2 spaces visible on each short end, 7 × 14 cm.

crochet.gaugeText: Finished granny rectangle measures 7 × 14 cm in DK-weight cotton with a 4 mm hook.

chartDefinition.title: Granny rectangle
chartDefinition.caption: Foundation chain sets the long axis. Corner clusters at the two short ends; cluster pairs along the long sides with ch-1 spaces. Three rounds.

glossaryTerms.definition: For a granny rectangle, the foundation chain sets the long axis. The first round works cluster pairs into the chain, with corner clusters at each end, to establish the rectangular outline.

content.text: The granny rectangle starts with a

rather than a magic ring, then works the first round along both sides of the chain with corner clusters at each end. From round 2 onward, the construction looks exactly like a granny square except the rectangle has two corners instead of four.
Add more clusters along the sides each round; the ends grow by one extra cluster pair per round. Three rounds give a 7 × 14 cm tile; five rounds give approximately 9 × 18 cm.

attrs.title: Materials for one motif
attrs.body: About 6 g of DK-weight cotton. A 4 mm hook. Tapestry needle and scissors.

content.text: 3 tr into 4th ch from hook (corner). Ch 1. *3 tr into next ch, ch 1*; rep 2 more times. Into last ch, work (3 tr, ch 2, 3 tr) corner. Working back along the other side of the chain: ch 1. *3 tr into ch, ch 1*; rep across. 3 tr into first ch. Ch 2. Sl st to top of first tr to join. (4 clusters per long side, 1 corner cluster each end.)

Sl st to corner sp. Ch 3. Work (2 tr, ch 2, 3 tr) into corner sp. *Ch 1, 3 tr into next ch-1 sp.* Rep across side. Into corner sp: (3 tr, ch 2, 3 tr). Continue around both sides and corners. Sl st to join.
Repeat round 2, adding one more cluster on each long side. Fasten off. (7 × 14 cm finished.)
Work the granny triangle next for a three-sided motif that fills the corner gaps when joining granny squares on the diagonal.
